title: Every second seat out
hook: 41 in a circle, every second one out. Who is left?

knows: recursion simplifies to a smaller case (hanoi-tower-doubles)
doesNotKnow: that a counting-out game has a closed form based on the binary of n

misconception: The survivor of a circle where every second person is removed is somewhere unpredictable; you have to simulate.
objective: The learner can explain that once the circle is down to a power of two the person the count starts on survives, so for 41 = 32 + 9 the survivor is 2·9 + 1 = 19, which is 41 in binary (101001) with its leading 1 moved to the end (010011).

claims.text: With 41 people and every second person removed, starting by skipping 1 (so 2, 4, ... go first), the survivor is 19.
claims.source: Demo.tsx play(41).survivor, which the stage and reveal print. Builder's node script (2026-10-14): removal order 2, 4, ..., 40, 1, 5, ...; survivor 19; after 38 removals 3, 19 and 35 remain. Recurrence J(1) = 1, J(2m) = 2J(m) - 1, J(2m + 1) = 2J(m) + 1 also gives 19. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): Own copy of play() (fc21/jo.mjs): order 2, 4, ..., 40, 1, 5, 9, 13, ...; survivor 19; after 38 removals 3, 19, 35 remain; recurrence J gives 19.

claims.text: After 9 removals 32 people are left and the count starts at 19 (reveal: 'Scrub to removal 9: 32 were left and the count started at 19'; key frame '32 left').
claims.source: Demo.tsx play(41): powFrame = 9 (first removal count that leaves a power of two), frames[9].skip = 19 (removed 2, 4, ..., 18). Builder's node script (2026-10-14) agrees. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): play(41): powFrame 9, 32 left, frames[9].skip = 19; reveal and key-frame label '32 left' match.

claims.text: With a power of two left, the person the count starts on always survives: each lap removes exactly half and comes back to them.
claims.source: With 2^m people and the count starting on person p (p is skipped), one lap removes every second person, 2^(m-1) of them, and the next count starts on p again; induct on m down to 1 person. Graham, Knuth and Patashnik, Concrete Mathematics (2nd ed.), section 1.3, J(2^m) = 1 (check before building: cited from the brief). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): Simulation: play(2^m) survivor 1 for m = 1..5, i.e. the starter. Induction argument holds. Concrete Mathematics 2e section 1.3 (Josephus problem, J(2^m) = 1) not opened; placement matches my knowledge.

claims.text: 41 = 32 + 9, so the survivor is 2 × 9 + 1 = 19; in binary 41 is 101001, and moving the leading 1 to the end gives 010011 = 19.
claims.source: Concrete Mathematics section 1.3: J(2^m + l) = 2l + 1 for 0 <= l < 2^m, and J((b_m b_(m-1) ... b_0)_2) = (b_(m-1) ... b_0 b_m)_2, a one-bit cyclic left shift (check before building: cited from the brief). Arithmetic: 41 = 0b101001, 0b010011 = 19 (node, 2026-10-14). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): node: 41 = 0b101001, rotated 0b010011 = 19; 2 x 9 + 1 = 19; formula J(2^m + l) = 2l + 1 checked against play(n) for every n < 200. GKP section 1.3 not opened (own knowledge agrees).

claims.text: 7 people leave 7 and 10 people leave 5 (table and reveal 'the same rule').
claims.source: Demo.tsx play(7) and play(10); builder's node script (2026-10-14): 7 -> 7 (4 left after 3 removals, count on 7), 10 -> 5 (8 left after 2 removals, count on 5). Formula: 7 = 4 + 3 -> 7, 10 = 8 + 2 -> 5. The brief's n = 7, k = 3 -> 4 uses a different skip and is not shown. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): play(7) -> 7 (4 left after 3 removals, starter 7); play(10) -> 5 (8 left after 2, starter 5); both match 2l + 1.

recall.question: 16 people stand in a circle numbered 1 to 16. Starting at 1, every second person is removed until one is left. Who survives?
recall.why: 16 is a power of two, so each lap removes exactly half and the count comes back to person 1 every time: 1 survives.
